title: How Dagobert Renouf bootstrapped Logology with a designer-in-the-loop quiz and Twitter memes
summary: Dagobert Renouf explains how he and his designer wife automated a $3,000 branding service into a roughly $100 logo product, and how Twitter (spam plugs, then personal story and memes) turned about one sale a week into six or seven. He also covers listening only to paying customers, staying focused on marketing over features, and building instead of reading.

principles.text: Productize a high-priced expert service by automating it and making it affordable.
principles.quote: we want to make what she does for three thousand dollars we want to automate it and make it affordable

principles.text: Remove bad outcomes by limiting and pre-vetting every choice the customer can make.
principles.quote: you can't go out of logology with a shitty looking logo it's not possible because we like limit every choice and vet every choice from her ahead of time

principles.text: Listen only to paying customers; non-buyers don't see the value and will pull your product off course.
principles.quote: we should only listen to people who pay us like people who actually spent money on the product

principles.text: When you don't know marketing, plug your product everywhere, then double down on the channel that works.
principles.quote: anytime there's the opportunity to plug in logology i'm gonna do it

principles.text: Personal-brand content on Twitter (story, memes) became the main sales driver.
principles.quote: growing on twitter was like the best thing i did because now i went from basically one sale per week to now about six or seven

principles.text: Resist building more features until marketing carries survival; keep saying no.
principles.quote: the whole thing for me is to say no i'm going to keep focusing on marketing
